title: Dependency ownership rotations and rollback safety net for roadmap cutovers
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Problem: Roadmap cutovers and release windows often suffer from unclear short-term ownership when multiple teams must coordinate (Eng, Design, Security, Infra). This results in slow responses to regressions and manual rollbacks that miss scope leading to production incidents or delayed launches. Goal: Create an operational pattern that (1) assigns a rotating short-term 'cutover owner' that can accept escalations across teams for a specified window, (2) automates rollback safety checks and circuit-breaker triggers tied to observability signals, and (3) surfaces ownership and rollback status through dashboards and calendar invites so stakeholders have one source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: Cutover owner rotation workflow created and documented in Confluence
Slack escalation flow implemented with a slash-command and automated paging to on-call during rotation windows
Automated rollback safety net: a deploy-time policy that can trigger a predefined rollback runbook when error-rate or latency SLO breaches exceed configured thresholds
Roadmap UI shows current cutover owner badge and active rollback state for any initiative in the release window
At least two cross-team dry runs completed with playbook verification and retrospective notes captured
proposed_solution: Ownership model: enforce a 72-hour rotation block per initiative. The PM assigns a primary and secondary cutover owner from Eng, with Design and Security liaisons assigned for advisory duties.

Automation: build a lightweight Cutover Orchestrator service (serverless) that schedules rotations, posts calendar events, and wires to Slack and PagerDuty. It will also subscribe to the Console telemetry stream for alert signals.

Rollback safety net: define a machine-readable rollback policy manifest for each release that includes SLO thresholds, rollback scope (service-level or route-level), and required approvals. Orchestrator can execute an automated rollback if thresholds are met and approvals are present; otherwise it initiates an urgent manual rollback paging path.
Visibility: extend roadmap dependency cards in Console to include 'Cutover owner', 'Rotation window', and 'Rollback status' metadata with links to runbooks and incident dashboards.
Testing: schedule two canary-cutover rehearsals per quarter where simulated regressions trigger the orchestrator to validate the end-to-end flow (notifications, circuit-breaker, and UI updates).
success_metrics: Mean time to acknowledge cutover incident reduced from 22m to <8m
Automated rollback accuracy: >= 90% successful scope-valid rollbacks during dry runs
Reduction in cross-team coordination tickets for cutover issues by 60% within one quarter
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize cutover owner rotation spec and publish Confluence playbook (PM + Eng + Design + Security)
Week 2: Implement Orchestrator MVP (scheduling, calendar, Slack hooks). Basic UI badge in Console shows rotation state.
Week 3: Add telemetry subscriptions and implement rollback policy engine (safe defaults only). Run an internal rehearsal with staging signals.
Week 4: Cross-team dry run with invited stakeholders; collect feedback and iterate playbook
Week 5: Gradual rollout: enable for a single mid-sized initiative, monitor metrics, then expand to all quarterly cutovers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-automation may trigger unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require secondary approval for high-risk services and default to manual for unknown services
Risk: Cutover owner burnout from repeated rotations. Mitigation: enforce max rotations per individual per quarter and provide a compensation buffer (time credit) policy
Risk: Slack/Pager noise during false positives. Mitigation: tune signal thresholds with historical telemetry and add a 'mute for 10m' quick action in Slack
Risk: Security-sensitive rollbacks may need privileged approvals. Mitigation: integrate KMS/approvals flow and add Security liaison as required approver for scoped policies
